questions.question: How long should the prepared presentation in the oral exam typically be?
options: 8-12 minutes
1-2 minutes
30-40 minutes
Exactly 20 minutes
questions.explanation: The prepared presentation typically lasts 8-12 minutes, followed by a 10-15 minute conversation.

questions.question: What structure is recommended for answering questions in the follow-up conversation?
options: Opinion → Reason → Example
Example → Joke → Conclusion
Question → Question → Question
Quote → Summary → Quote
questions.explanation: State your opinion, give a reason, and support it with an example — a clear way to give substantial answers.

questions.question: What should the opening of your presentation contain?
options: A hook, your topic and a preview of your main points
A detailed history of the topic
An apology for being nervous
All your conclusions at once
questions.explanation: A strong opening (1-2 minutes) hooks the audience, introduces the topic and previews the structure.

questions.question: Which is good advice for body language during a presentation?
options: Make eye contact, keep an open posture and vary your voice
Look at your notes the whole time
Speak in a flat monotone to seem calm
Stand completely still with arms crossed
questions.explanation: Eye contact, open posture, natural gestures and vocal variety make your delivery engaging — avoid monotone.

questions.question: What is the number one tip for oral exam preparation?
options: Practise speaking English aloud every day in the weeks before
Memorise your presentation word for word
Read silently as much as possible
Avoid English until the exam day
questions.explanation: Daily speaking practice — talking to yourself, recording yourself, practising with others — builds the fluency examiners assess.
